_note: Sitting Mississippi, Vermont, Michigan and Tennessee state legislators, read on 2026-10-28. Mississippi from the Open States current-legislator list (compiled from the Legislature's own member pages), checked against the Legislature's member XML and Wikipedia's chamber records: the Legislature's XML still lists members the November 2025 court-ordered special elections replaced, and Open States carries the winners. Vermont from the Legislature's own member list (legislature.vermont.gov/people/loadAll/2026), current members only: it seats the eleven members appointed since the 2025 session, whom Open States has not caught up with. Michigan and Tennessee were already on the roster (db/roster-state-legislators-mi-nj-va-2026-oct.json, db/roster-state-legislators-tn-in-mo-2026-oct.json); Tennessee's two House vacancies are the chamber directory's (House 31, Ron Travis, who resigned on election as Rhea County executive, which Open States still seats; House 84). cmp-data.js carries a roster shell for every "rows" entry; "alreadyHeld" are existing records that already named the seat; "seatedFromCandidacy" names sitting members who were on the roster only as a 2026 federal or statewide candidacy — their row now names the seat they hold and the candidacy moved to window.CMP_CANDIDACIES; "usHouseDistrictSet" names U.S. Representatives whose row gained its district. VERMONT'S SEATS: the Senate elects 30 members from 16 county districts and the House 150 from 109 districts, each district one, two or three members. A district's own name is its seat (the resolver keys it by its place in TIGERweb's 2024 list); a district with one member is one board, keyed like any other seat; a district with two or three is one board per member, keyed by position (vt-statehouse-1-p1, as Washington's, Idaho's and South Dakota's House seats are keyed). Vermont numbers no seat in such a district, so the positions are PolitiDex's, in surname order, printed Seat A, Seat B, Seat C; "membersPerDistrict" is the count each district elects, and it matches the 2026 ballot's vote-for count in every district. Mississippi Rep. Jeffrey Hulum III (House 119) was on the roster as the MS-4 Democratic nominee; his row now names his House seat. Four Mississippi and Vermont senators already carried an id in state-senate-stances-w10.js and -w12.js (dean_kirby, derrick_simmons, phil_baruth, kesha_ram_hinsdale); their shells use it. Mississippi Sen. Mike Thompson (thompson_ms) is not California's U.S. Rep. Mike Thompson (mike_thompson).
